Subject: RE: [ie-rant] Re: The Nerd-out continues, now its perso... (sorry)... Vista

I'm using the Vista Ultimate (64Bit). I had 2GB of ram and it just didn't run as good as I'd hoped it would, I had disabled indexing on the file and email. It just wastes resources.
 
I now have 4GB of ram , and it runs much better, its faster at opening apps, the real test was processing video, which was great with the extra ram. The system would normally use 1.6GB of the available ram with only a few apps open. Put in 4GB if you can,
 
1.6 GHz dual core should be fine, if its the 32bit version of Vista, the max amount of ram you can have is 4GB, if its the 64Bit, you can add more, I'm not sure what the limit is.
 
As for the waiting for SP1, SP1 is a bit of a PR stunt from MS, a lot of companies wait till SP1 is released, but realistically the updates in SP1 are available from Windows Update.
 
The issues with the file transfer are fixed with a patch. I had that problem but got the patch and it sorted it out. I'm using Vista now for about 6 months, I'm impressed with it, it still does Blue Screen but then I push the machine to the limits testing software etc. But overall its a good OS. 
 
On a similar note the new Windows Longhorn (Server 2008) is pretty good as well, it will work very well with Vista.  It's a breeze to install, I'm running the server online with a HL2 server on it and it runs really well. 
 
g
